Search for a 630 GeV Resonance in the Di-Photon
Channel with an Upgraded Tracker
M. Horák, J. Lindqvist, A. Ramirez, P. Novotný, and the HEP-UPG Collaboration
Journal of Instrumentation — Proceedings of the 21st Pisa Meeting on Advanced Detectors
Abstract
A search for a narrow scalar resonance decaying into two photons is presented, using 139 fb-1 of proton–proton
collisions at √s = 13 TeV recorded with the upgraded inner tracker. The di-photon invariant mass spectrum is fitted
with a parametric background model whose uncertainty is constrained in three control regions. An excess is observed at
mγγ = 630. 4 ± 1. 1 GeV with a local significance of 5. 8 standard deviations, corresponding to 1. 4 standard…
Introduction
Extensions of the Standard Model with an additional scalar singlet predict narrow resonances that couple to photons
through a loop of charged particles. Searches in the di-photon final state are therefore among the most sensitive
probes of such scenarios at the LHC . The published analysis of the 2022 dataset was limited by the forward
acceptance of the previous tracking detector, where the occupancy at η > 2 degraded the reconstruction efficiency…
Detector and Dataset
The inner tracker consists of four pixel layers at radii between 32 mm and 96 mm, each providing a single-point
resolution of 12 µm and designed to withstand a fluence of 3 × 1015 neq/cm^2. Photon candidates are reconstructed
from topological clusters in the electromagnetic calorimeter and required to have E_T > 25 GeV and η < 2. 37,…
Event Selection
Photons are required to be isolated, with the scalar sum of transverse energy in a cone of Δ R = 0. 4 below 6 GeV
after subtracting the expected pile-up contribution. The two leading photons must be separated by Δ R > 0. 4 and
satisfy Σ p_T < 20 GeV to reject events with significant jet activity. Table 1 lists the cumulative cut flow.
Background Model
The dominant background is irreducible prompt di-photon production, whose invariant mass spectrum is smooth and well
described by a fourth-order Bernstein polynomial. The fit is performed over the range 550–750 GeV while the signal
window is blinded; the number of parameters is chosen by an F-test on the sidebands, and the residual bias of the
fit is estimated with pseudo-experiments. Systematic uncertainty from the background model is taken as the envelope…
Results
The fitted signal-plus-background model is shown in Figure 2. The excess corresponds to a signal yield of 41 ± 8
events, with a fitted mass of 630. 4 ± 1. 1 GeV and a width consistent with the detector resolution of 1. 6 GeV. The
local p-value of the background-only hypothesis is 3 × 10-9, i. e. 5. 8 standard deviations; accounting for the…
